stories.title: Floating Points Headlines Refuge Saturday Oct. 24
stories.dek: The British producer Floating Points tops the bill at Refuge's Saturday night party in Brooklyn on Oct. 24.
body: Floating Points is the headliner at Refuge on Saturday, Oct. 24, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The night is part of the Brooklyn club's regular Saturday series.
The listing says doors open at 10 p.m. and the party runs until 5 a.m. Sunday. Refuge is located at 366 Ten Eyck Street in Brooklyn.

Floating Points is the only artist named on the bill, and the listing does not give a full lineup or set times. The event is tagged as house and techno, and the listing promotes the series with the tagline "Before. During. Afters."
The listing does not post a ticket price or an age policy. Tickets are sold through Eventbrite, according to the page.

stories.title: Victor Calderone Leads Refuge's All-Day Halloween Party Oct. 31
stories.dek: Refuge in Brooklyn opens at 6 a.m. on Halloween for a 16-hour session with Victor Calderone and Anthony Middleton.
body: Refuge is holding an all-day party on Saturday, Oct. 31, with DJs Victor Calderone and Anthony Middleton, according to an event listing on The Best Parties.
The event, billed as PURGATORY: Saturday All Day, starts at 6 a.m. and runs until 10 p.m., the listing says. It takes place at the club at 366 Ten Eyck Street in Brooklyn.

The session is part of a larger Halloween run at the club that the listing describes as six parties over four days. Other listings on the same site point to a follow-on PURGATORY sunrise session at Refuge on Sunday morning.
Calderone and Middleton are the only artists named, and the event is tagged as house and techno. The listing does not give a ticket price or an age policy. Tickets are sold through Eventbrite.

sources.title: PURGATORY: Saturday All Day @ Refuge w/ Victor Calderone, Anthony Middleton

stories.title: L7 Brings 'Last Hurrah' Farewell Tour to Knockdown Center Oct. 24
stories.dek: The Los Angeles rock band plays Maspeth on the first leg of what it has called its farewell world tour.
body: L7 plays Knockdown Center in Maspeth, Queens, on Saturday, Oct. 24, as part of The Last Hurrah Tour, according to an event listing on The Best Parties.
The listing says the show runs from 6 p.m. to 10 p.m. at the venue at 52-19 Flushing Avenue. Tickets start at $51 and are sold through DICE. The page does not list opening acts or an age policy.
BrooklynVegan reported in May that the tour is the first leg of the band's farewell world tour. L7 formed in 1985, was active until 2001 and reunited in 2015, according to that report.

The fall North American run began in Phoenix on Oct. 9, BrooklynVegan reported. After New York, the band is scheduled to play Boston on Oct. 26 and Detroit on Oct. 31, with the leg ending in Los Angeles on Nov. 14.

sources.title: L7 announce farewell tour (BV presale for NYC)

stories.title: Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical Bring Helado Tropical to Knockdown Center
stories.dek: The new duo plays Maspeth on Sunday, Oct. 25, with Nick Hakim also on the bill.
body: Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical perform together as Helado Tropical at Knockdown Center in Maspeth, Queens, on Sunday, Oct. 25, according to an event listing on The Best Parties.
The listing says the show runs from 6 p.m. to 10 p.m. at 52-19 Flushing Avenue, with Nick Hakim also on the bill and additional acts not named. Tickets start at $38. No age policy is listed.

Helado Negro is the stage name of producer and singer-songwriter Roberto Carlos Lange, and Reyna Tropical is the project of guitarist and songwriter Fabi Reyna, The World from PRX reported in August. The two met in 2024 and later formed the duo, whose debut album shares the band's name and is sung in Spanish, according to that report.
The duo's U.S. tour began in San Diego on Aug. 12 and is set to end in Mexico City in November, The World reported.

sources.title: Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical Present: HELADO TROPICAL w/ Nick Hakim +
A new duo, Helado Tropical, makes experimental Latin pop with love and laughs

stories.title: Circoloco Halloween Weekend Set as Final Nights at Brooklyn Storehouse
stories.dek: The two-night party on Oct. 30 and 31 is listed as sold out, as the Navy Yard venue prepares to close and its promoter faces a court order.
body: Circoloco's Halloween weekend at Brooklyn Storehouse in the Brooklyn Navy Yard runs Oct. 30 and 31, and the Friday night is listed as sold out on The Best Parties. The Friday party runs from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., the listing says.

The lineup for the first night includes Mochakk, Beltran, Rampa, Carlita and Seth Troxler, while the Halloween night features ANOTR, Dixon, Rossi. and Jimi Jules, among others, EDM Identity reported in August. The events are presented by Circoloco and Teksupport.
Brooklyn Storehouse is closing after Oct. 31, Resident Advisor reported. The venue opened in 2024 as a temporary space inside the Navy Yard, according to EDM Identity.

Resident Advisor also reported on Oct. 7 that a New Jersey court ordered TCE Presents, the parent company of Teksupport, to cease operations, barring it from holding events under its brands starting Nov. 7. The outlet said at the time it was unclear whether the Oct. 30 and 31 parties would go ahead. Ticket holders should check with the seller, DICE, for updates.

sources.title: CircoLoco NYC 2026 Lineup: Beltran, Mochakk, ANOTR, and More
New York promoter Teksupport and parent firm ordered to cease operations

stories.title: Kaytranada Plays Pacha NYC on Halloween Eve
stories.dek: The producer headlines the Brooklyn club on Friday, Oct. 30, with tickets starting at about $222.
body: Kaytranada headlines Pacha NYC on Friday, Oct. 30, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The show runs from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m.

The club is located at 140 Stewart Avenue in Brooklyn, the listing says. Pacha New York relaunched in Brooklyn in June as the first North American outpost of the Ibiza-based club brand, Resident reported.
Kaytranada is the only artist listed for the night, and the event is tagged as electronic. Tickets start at about $222, according to the listing.

The club held a pre-opening weekend on June 13 and 14 curated by Rampa, and its fall calendar has included BLOND:ISH in September and a Miss Monique night set for Nov. 13, Resident reported. The Best Parties listing also points readers to an all-day PURGATORY party at Refuge in Brooklyn the following morning.
The page does not state an age policy or give set times.

sources.title: Pacha New York Is Building Its Summer and Fall Calendar in Brooklyn

stories.title: Purple Disco Machine Plays Pacha NYC on Halloween Night
stories.dek: The German producer headlines the Brooklyn club on Saturday, Oct. 31, with tickets from about $169.
body: Purple Disco Machine headlines Pacha NYC on Saturday, Oct. 31, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The party runs from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m.
The club is at 140 Stewart Avenue in Brooklyn, the listing says. Pacha New York opened in Brooklyn in June as the Ibiza-based brand's first North American club, Resident reported.
Purple Disco Machine is the only artist named for the night, and the event is tagged as electronic. Tickets start at about $169, according to the listing.

The page does not give an age policy or set times. The Halloween date follows a Kaytranada show at the same club on Friday, Oct. 30, and comes ahead of a Miss Monique night at the club on Nov. 13, according to Resident.

stories.title: Lost Frequencies Plays Marquee New York Oct. 30
stories.dek: The Belgian DJ headlines the Chelsea club on the Friday before Halloween; entry is 21 and over.
body: Lost Frequencies plays Marquee New York on Friday, Oct. 30, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The night runs from 11 p.m. to 4 a.m.
Marquee is located at 289 10th Avenue in Chelsea, the listing says. Lost Frequencies is the only artist named on the bill, and the night is tagged as hip-hop and open format.
Entry is by table reservation or general admission, and guests must be 21 or older, according to the listing. The page does not post a ticket price. Tickets are sold through a link on the listing.

The club follows the show with a Halloween night on Saturday, Oct. 31, headlined by the DJ duo Two Friends, according to a separate listing on the same site. For those continuing into the weekend, the listing points to an all-day PURGATORY party at Refuge in Brooklyn, with Victor Calderone and Anthony Middleton, running from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Saturday.

sources.title: Lost Frequencies at Marquee New York

stories.title: Two Friends Headline Marquee New York on Halloween
stories.dek: The DJ duo plays the Chelsea club on Saturday, Oct. 31, from 11 p.m.; entry is 21 and over.
body: The DJ duo Two Friends headlines Marquee New York on Halloween night, Saturday, Oct. 31, according to an event listing on The Best Parties. The night runs from 11 p.m. to 4 a.m. on Nov. 1.
Marquee is at 289 10th Avenue in Chelsea, the listing says. Two Friends is the only act named for the night, which is tagged as hip-hop and open format.

Entry is by table reservation or general admission, and guests must be 21 or older, according to the listing. No ticket price is posted on the page. Tickets are sold through the Tao Group ticketing site.

The Halloween show follows a Friday, Oct. 30, set at the club by Belgian DJ Lost Frequencies. The listing also points to a PURGATORY sunrise session with Mira at Refuge in Brooklyn, running from 6 a.m. to noon on Sunday.

stories.title: Blakeman Uses Fatal Midtown Subway Shooting to Attack Hochul
stories.dek: The Republican nominee for governor rode the subway to the station where a man was killed, while Hochul's campaign pointed to state spending on subway policing.
body: Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman on Monday used a fatal weekend shooting at a Midtown subway station to attack Gov. Kathy Hochul's record on public safety, NY1 reported.

Blakeman rode the subway from his Long Island home to the Seventh Avenue station near West 53rd Street, where police say an argument between two men ended with a 26-year-old man shot dead, according to NY1. The suspect had not been caught when NY1 published its report.

Blakeman accused Hochul of pulling police from subway platforms and called for more officers in the system, better lighting at the station and more conductors on trains, NY1 reported. He told reporters a police presence might have deterred the attack.

Hochul's campaign pointed to two years of state money dedicated to NYPD overtime and overnight subway patrols, according to NY1. A campaign spokeswoman said the governor had invested a record $4 billion in policing. Mayor Zohran Mamdani, at a separate Bronx event, accused Blakeman of exploiting New Yorkers' fears for political gain.
NYPD officials have cited overall declines in crime, including on the subway, but seven deaths have been recorded in the system this year, compared with four last year, NY1 reported.

sources.title: Blakeman uses fatal subway shooting as campaign cudgel against Hochul
